events.title: Establishment of the Club of Rome
events.description: A meeting of international professionals in a villa in Rome led by Aurelio Peccei and Alexander King resulted in the creation of the Club of Rome, a think‑tank focused on resource consumption and global limits.
actors: International group of professionals from industry, academia and civil society
events.supporting_text: In 1968, the industrialist Aurelio Peccei (1908-84) and Scottish scientist Alexander King (1909-2007) invited an international group of professionals from industry, academia and civil society to a villa in Rome. ... Following the meeting, the participants established the Club of Rome as a focal point for their shared concerns.

events.title: Publication of The Limits to Growth
events.description: The Club of Rome released its first report, "The Limits to Growth," presenting scenarios from an integrated global model linking world economy and environment, highlighting potential future limits to growth.
actors: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) systems scientists
events.supporting_text: The Club's first report, The Limits to Growth (1972), was underpinned by the work of a group of systems scientists at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), who had developed the first integrated global model linking the world economy and the environment.

events.title: Publication of The Ultimate Resource
events.description: Julian Simon published "The Ultimate Resource," arguing that human ingenuity and substitution would overcome physical resource limits, challenging the limits‑to‑growth perspective.
events.supporting_text: Julian Simon (1932-98) was among the most prominent academics to challenge the idea that there are physical limits to resources that must ultimately constrain economic growth. His arguments were summarised in The Ultimate Resource (1981).

events.title: Ehrlich–Simon metal price wager
events.description: Paul R. Ehrlich and Julian Simon made a public bet on the price trends of five metals from 1980 to 1990; Ehrlich predicted rising prices, Simon predicted falling prices, and Simon won the wager.
events.supporting_text: Simon also entered a wager with Ehrlich regarding the prices of five metals. Ehrlich predicted prices of each metal would rise between 1980 and 1990, demonstrating their growing scarcity. Simon predicted they would fall as technology and substitution would keep prices low. Simon won the bet...

events.title: Publication of The Entropy Law and the Economic Process
events.description: Nicholas Georgescu‑Roegen published his seminal work *The Entropy Law and the Economic Process*, introducing the idea that the use of energy reduces the amount of usable energy available to society and linking the second law of thermodynamics to economic theory.
events.supporting_text: In The Entropy Law and the Economic Process (1971), Georgescu-Roegen explained that whenever energy is used, the amount of usable energy available to society declines.

events.title: Publication of Small is Beautiful: A Study of Economics as if People Mattered
events.description: Ernst F. Schumacher published *Small is Beautiful*, championing appropriate technology and arguing that natural resources should be treated as capital rather than as expandable income.
events.supporting_text: Ernst F. Schumacher (1911-77), who championed the use of appropriate technology in Small is Beautiful: A Study of Economics as if People Mattered (1973).

events.title: Launch of World Bank Natural Wealth Accounting Plan
events.description: The World Bank, supported by India, Mexico and several other countries, launched a plan to create an accounting framework that places the natural wealth of nations alongside traditional financial measurements such as GDP.
events.supporting_text: In 2010 the World Bank launched a plan, backed by India, Mexico and a number of other countries, to create an accounting measure that puts the natural wealth of nations alongside financial measurements such as GDP.

events.title: Beaver Committee cost assessment of air pollution
events.description: An early attempt at costing the damage caused by air pollution was made by the Beaver Committee, estimating economic losses of hundreds of millions of pounds from infrastructure, buildings, laundry, and reduced economic efficiency.
events.supporting_text: An early attempt at costing the damage caused by air pollution was made by the Beaver Committee in the mid-1950s (see Chapter 4).

events.title: Roskill Commission proposal for third runway in London
events.description: The Roskill Commission proposed a location for a third runway in London and used social cost‑benefit analysis to support its case, with noise pollution as a major contested issue.
events.supporting_text: When the Roskill Commission proposed a location for a third runway in London in the early 1970s, it used social cost‑benefit analysis to support its case.

events.title: Publication of MIT report "Man's Impact on the Global Environment"
events.description: A 1970 MIT report of the Study of Critical Environmental Problems described nine 'environmental services' that would decline if ecosystem functioning were damaged, laying groundwork for the ecosystem‑services concept.
events.supporting_text: An 1970 MIT report of the Study of Critical Environmental Problems, entitled Man's Impact on the Global Environment: Assessment and Recommendations for Action, described nine 'environmental services' that would decline if the functioning of ecosystems were damaged.

events.title: Millennium Ecosystem Assessment
events.description: A global, multi‑year assessment that examined the consequences of ecosystem change on human wellbeing, providing an overview of ecosystem conditions and defining four categories of ecosystem services.
events.supporting_text: It was then used as a central organising concept for the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment, undertaken between 2001 and 2005. The Millennium Ecosystem Assessment examined the consequences of ecosystem change on human wellbeing, and provided a global overview of conditions of the world's ecosystems and the services they provide to humanity.

events.title: Robert Costanza et al. estimate of global ecosystem services value
events.description: In the late 1980s, Robert Costanza and colleagues attempted to estimate the monetary value of ecosystem services provided by the Earth's biosphere, arriving at a range of US$16‑54 trillion per year.
events.supporting_text: However, in the late 1980s Robert Costanza and colleagues attempted to estimate the value of ecosystem services provided by the Earth's biosphere. They estimated the value of the services provided by the ecosystem to humanity at between US$16‑54 trillion per year.

events.title: Development and application of ecosystem services concept
events.description: Throughout the 1980s and 1990s the ecosystem‑services idea was further developed and applied to biodiversity assessments, expanding its use in environmental policy and research.
events.supporting_text: Throughout the 1980s and 1990s, the idea was developed further, applied to biodiversity assessments, and then used as a central organising concept for the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment.

events.title: Publication of the Stern Review
events.description: The 2006 Stern Review presented a high‑profile economic case for environmental action, arguing that the cost of inaction on climate change would exceed the cost of mitigation and highlighting the importance of low discount rates for future generations.
events.supporting_text: The 2006 Stern Review is the most highprofile example of economic theory presenting the case for environmental action.

events.title: Publication of UNEP report on corporate environmental damage
events.description: A United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) report estimated that 3,000 listed companies were responsible for US$2.15 trillion worth of environmental damage in 2008, with greenhouse‑gas emissions accounting for about 70 % of the total externalities valued.
events.supporting_text: In 2010, a UNEP report estimated that 3000 listed companies were responsible for US$2.15 trillion worth of environmental damage in 2008, equivalent to 7 per cent off their combined revenues.

events.title: Deepwater Horizon oil spill
events.description: The Deepwater Horizon oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico caused extensive environmental damage; BP incurred substantial cleanup costs, illustrating the real‑world economic impact of ecological liabilities.
events.supporting_text: The costs incurred by the global oil and gas company BP in cleaning up the 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico illustrate the real-world economic impact of ecological liabilities.

events.title: Publication of "The Tragedy of the Commons"
events.description: Garrett Hardin introduced the concept of the "tragedy of the commons," using the analogy of shared grazing land to explain how unregulated common resources lead to over‑use and environmental degradation.
events.supporting_text: In 1967, Garrett Hardin (1915-2003) developed the notion of the 'tragedy of the commons' where he used the analogy of common grazing land to illustrate that sharing common resources leads to over-use.

events.title: International Conference on Water and the Environment
events.description: A 1992 conference where participants agreed that water has an economic value in all its competing uses and should be recognised as an economic good, supporting the ecosystem services approach and water pricing.
actors: International Conference on Water and the Environment
events.supporting_text: In 1992, the International Conference on Water and the Environment agreed that 'water has an economic value in all its competing uses and should be recognised as an economic good'.

events.title: Electoral victory of Evo Morales
events.description: Following protests against water privatisation in Cochabamba, a political upheaval propelled indigenous leader Evo Morales to win the national election in Bolivia.
events.supporting_text: When a privately run water company increased the price of water and sanitation in the Bolivian town of Cochabamba, this set in motion a chain of protests against privatisation and a political upheaval that swept the indigenous people's leader Evo Morales (b. 1959) to electoral victory in 2003.

events.title: Global financial crisis
events.description: The worldwide financial crisis of 2008‑2009 caused a contraction in global per‑capita income and a decline in world trade volumes, creating a context for environmental advocacy of a green recovery.
events.supporting_text: The 2008-09 global financial crisis led to global per capita income contracting and the volume of world trade declining.

events.title: Launch of Global Green New Deal (GGND) initiative
events.description: UNEP launched the Global Green New Deal in December 2008, proposing an economic stimulus package aimed at reviving the global economy, creating jobs, reducing carbon dependency, and ending extreme poverty by 2015.
events.supporting_text: Following in his footsteps, UNEP instigated the Global Green New Deal (GGND) initiative in December 2008.

events.title: G20 London Summit
events.description: The United Kingdom's Labour Prime Minister Gordon Brown convened the G20 leaders in London to discuss the international response to the financial crisis and to commit to a transition toward clean, innovative, resource‑efficient, low‑carbon technologies and sustainable economies.
events.supporting_text: In April 2009, UK's then Labour Prime Minister Gordon Brown (b. 1951) held the G20 London Summit to discuss the international response to the financial crisis. A G20 communiqué from the meeting stated 'We will make the transition towards clean, innovative, resource efficient, low carbon technologies and infrastructure [...] We will identify and work together on further measures to build sustainable economies.'

events.title: G20 Pittsburgh Summit
events.description: At the September 2009 summit in Pittsburgh, the G20 pledged to enhance global climate‑change initiatives, improve energy security, phase out fossil‑fuel subsidies and reduce the vulnerability of the world’s poor.
events.supporting_text: At the September 2009 Pittsburgh Summit, the G20 further pledged to enhance global climate change initiatives, improve energy security and phase out fossil fuel subsidies as well as reduce the vulnerability of the world's poor.

events.title: Launch of the UK Green Economy Budget
events.description: The United Kingdom allocated roughly 11 % of its US$3.9 billion fiscal stimulus to green investments and introduced a ‘Green economy’ budget in April 2009, targeting low‑carbon projects intended to create 400,000 new jobs over eight years.
events.supporting_text: The UK devoted approximately 11 per cent of its US$3.9 billion fiscal stimulus to green investments as well as launching a 'Green economy' budget in April 2009, which included a range of low-carbon investments aimed at creating 400,000 new jobs over an eight-year period.

events.title: Adoption of the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act
events.description: The United States enacted a US$78.5 billion recovery package in February 2009 that incorporated measures to retrofit buildings, expand mass transit, freight rail, renewable energy and to build a smart electrical‑grid transmission system.
events.supporting_text: In February 2009, the USA adopted a US$78.5 billion American Recovery and Reinvestment Act, which included measures to retrofit buildings and expand mass transit, freight rail and renewable energy as well as construct a 'smart' electrical grid transmission system.

events.title: Publication of "Towards a Green Economy: Pathways to Sustainable Development and Poverty Eradication"
events.description: UNEP released a report in February 2011 advocating green investment worldwide, linking green economies to poverty eradication and outlining investment recommendations across ten key sectors.
events.supporting_text: In February 2011, UNEP published Towards a Green Economy: Pathways to Sustainable Development and Poverty Eradication, which further advocated green investment on a global scale.

events.title: G20 Green Stimulus Spending During the Recession
events.description: Throughout the global recession, G20 members collectively spent over US$520 billion on green stimulus measures, representing 16 % of all fiscal spending and 0.7 % of G20 GDP, though falling short of the 1 % GGND recommendation.
events.supporting_text: During the recession, members of the G20 spent over US$520 billion on a green stimulus. The stimulus comprised 16 per cent of all fiscal spending and 0.7 per cent of the G20 GDP, falling short of the 1 per cent GGND recommendation.

events.title: Publication of *Prosperity Without Growth*
events.description: Tim Jackson’s book argues for a different kind of economy that allows human flourishing within ecological limits, critiquing growth‑driven consumerism and calling for a transition to clean, renewable energy technologies.
events.supporting_text: In Prosperity Without Growth (2009), Tim Jackson argues that a different kind of economy is essential for a different kind of prosperity - one where human beings can flourish within the ecological limits of a finite planet.

events.title: Rio+20 United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development
events.description: The international community’s attention turns to the Rio+20 summit, a high‑level conference that focuses on integrating green‑economy strategies with poverty‑reduction goals.
events.supporting_text: as the international community turns its attention to Rio+20.

events.title: End of food rationing in the United Kingdom
events.description: All food rationing in the UK was terminated, marking the end of wartime and post‑war rationing policies.
events.supporting_text: it was not until July 1954 that all food rationing in the UK came to an end.

events.title: Opening of the Preston by‑pass
events.description: The Preston by‑pass was opened, inaugurating the ‘motorway age’ in Britain.
events.supporting_text: the 'motorway age' was born when the Preston by‑pass was opened in December 1958

events.title: Opening of the M1 motorway
events.description: The M1, the first long stretch of inter‑urban motorway in the UK, was opened, further expanding the national road network.
events.supporting_text: followed in November 1959 by the M1, the first long stretch of inter‑urban motorway.

events.title: Publication of *Unsafe at Any Speed*
events.description: Ralph Nader published a book exposing the automobile industry's resistance to improving vehicle pollution and safety, sparking a new wave of consumer advocacy.
events.supporting_text: In 1965, Ralph Nader (b. 1934) published Unsafe at Any Speed, which examined the reluctance of the car industry to improve both vehicle pollution and safety.

events.title: Launch of ITV, the first independent television station in the UK
events.description: ITV began broadcasting, ending the BBC's monopoly and introducing commercial television advertising to British audiences.
events.supporting_text: Two years later, the BBC's monopoly of television came to an end when the first independent television station, ITV, went on air.

events.title: Coronation of Queen Elizabeth II
events.description: The coronation ceremony of Queen Elizabeth II took place, prompting many British families to purchase their first television sets.
events.supporting_text: In 1953 many families in the UK bought their first television for the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II.

events.title: Publication of "The Affluent Society"
events.description: Economist J. K. Galbraith published his book *The Affluent Society*, identifying the imbalance between newly‑found private wealth and its environmental effects.
events.supporting_text: The economist J. K. Galbraith (1908-2006) eloquently identified the imbalance between the new‑found private wealth and its environmental effects in his book The Affluent Society (1956).

events.title: Cuyahoga River oil slick fire (media coverage)
events.description: Television coverage of the 1969 oil slick fire on the Cuyahoga River highlighted the human impact on the environment and helped raise public awareness of pollution.
events.supporting_text: Coverage of the 1969 oil slick fire on the Cuyahoga River ... were key moments in the growing media coverage of the human impact on the environment.

events.title: Santa Barbara Channel oil spill (media coverage)
events.description: Media reporting on the Santa Barbara Channel oil spill contributed to growing public concern about environmental damage caused by industrial accidents.
events.supporting_text: ... and the Santa Barbara Channel oil spill were key moments in the growing media coverage of the human impact on the environment.

events.title: Capture of the first Earthrise image by Apollo 8 crew
events.description: On Christmas Eve, 24 December 1968, the Apollo 8 crew photographed Earth rising over the lunar landscape, creating the iconic “Earthrise” image that later influenced environmental consciousness.
events.supporting_text: The first pictures of Earth from space were actually taken by the crew of Apollo 8 eight months earlier, on Christmas Eve in December 1968... The first image of Earth rising in the vast darkness of space over a lunar landscape became an iconic picture. ... the image became known as 'Earthrise'.

events.title: Apollo 11 Moon landing
events.description: On 20 July 1969 the US lunar module Eagle landed on the Moon; extensive television coverage and the iconic images of Earth from space helped bring modern environmental concepts into the mainstream.
events.supporting_text: What had been a dream for many people, ... became a reality on 20 July 1969 when the US lunar module Eagle successfully landed on the moon's surface. ... the extensive television coverage of humanity's first mission to land on the moon, and the images of planet Earth from space, also helped to bring modern environmental concepts into the mainstream.

events.title: Proposal of the first Earth Day by Senator Gaylord Nelson
events.description: On 22 April 1970 US Senator Gaylord Nelson proposed the first Earth Day, which was marked by a nationwide teach‑in involving schools, colleges, universities and community groups, and attracted an estimated 20 million participants.
events.supporting_text: A year after the moon landing, US senator Gaylord Nelson (1916-2005) proposed the first Earth Day on 22 April 1970. The day was marked by a national environment teach‑in led by schools, colleges, universities and community groups. Media coverage included a primetime CBS News Special Report called Earth Day: A Question of Survival.

events.title: Broadcast of CBS News Special Report "Earth Day: A Question of Survival"
events.description: A primetime CBS News special report aired during the first Earth Day, focusing on the survival of the planet and highlighting environmental challenges.
events.supporting_text: Media coverage included a primetime CBS News Special Report called Earth Day: A Question of Survival.

events.title: Founding of Keep America Beautiful
events.description: Keep America Beautiful (KAB) was founded by a group of US corporate and civic leaders to promote and develop a national cleanliness ethic in response to the growing problem of litter.
events.supporting_text: KAB was founded in 1953 by a group of US corporate and civic leaders to promote and develop a national cleanliness ethic in response to the growing problem of litter.

events.title: First public service announcement on litter prevention by Keep America Beautiful
events.description: Keep America Beautiful produced its first public service announcement aimed at preventing litter.
events.supporting_text: in 1956 it produced its first public service announcement on litter prevention.

events.title: Earth Day campaign (1970)
events.description: The Earth Day campaign highlighted the need for individuals and communities to protect the environment.
events.supporting_text: By 1970, the Earth Day campaign was again highlighting the need for individuals and communities to do their bit to protect the environment.

events.title: Launch of the 'Crying Indian' public announcement campaign
events.description: Keep America Beautiful launched the iconic 'Crying Indian' TV advert to promote personal environmental responsibility.
events.supporting_text: In 1971, Keep America Beautiful (KAB) launched the 'Crying Indian' public announcement campaign, which was to become an iconic symbol of personal environmental responsibility.

events.title: Adoption of Oregon Bottle Bill
events.description: The State of Oregon passed a landmark Bottle Bill requiring a five‑cent deposit on beer and soft‑drink containers to reduce litter and conserve resources.
events.supporting_text: in 1971 the State of Oregon's landmark Bottle Bill became law in spite of intense lobbying by container and beverage industries.

events.title: Proposal of California Bottle Bill
events.description: The State of California proposed a bottle‑deposit bill similar to Oregon’s, which faced public opposition from Keep America Beautiful.
events.supporting_text: In 1974, the State of California proposed a similar bill but KAB publicly opposed it

events.title: Launch of Clean Community System
events.description: Keep America Beautiful introduced the Clean Community System, emphasizing street cleaning and other litter‑control activities as an alternative to bottle‑deposit legislation.
events.supporting_text: and a year later launched the Clean Community System as an alternative that placed an emphasis on street cleaning and other litter-control activities.

events.title: Materials recovery program launched in Woodbury, New Jersey
events.description: Woodbury became the first U.S. city to begin a materials‑recovery (recycling) program, led by a local community organization.
events.supporting_text: In November 1970, Woodbury, New Jersey was the first US city to begin materials recovery, spearheaded by an environmentally concerned community organisation.

events.title: Ecology Center recycling demonstration project in Berkeley
events.description: The Ecology Center launched a newspaper‑collection recycling demonstration in Berkeley, which served as a model for municipal recycling programmes.
events.supporting_text: In 1973, the Ecology Center, a US action-orientated organisation, launched a recycling demonstration project in Berkeley, California collecting newspapers, which became a model for other municipal recycling programmes.

events.title: Installation of UK's first bottle bank at Tesco, Barnsley
events.description: The UK's first bottle bank was installed in the car park of a Tesco supermarket in Barnsley, South Yorkshire, introduced by Stanley Race to promote glass recycling.
events.supporting_text: In August 1977, the UK's first bottle bank was sited in the car park of the Tesco supermarket in Barnsley, South Yorkshire. The bottle bank was introduced by Stanley Race, then president of the Glass Manufacturers' Federation, with the aim of convincing local authorities that such schemes could be environmentally friendly and pay for themselves.

events.title: 1973 OPEC oil export embargo
events.description: Major Arab oil‑producing states imposed an oil export embargo through OPEC, causing a hike in oil prices and an oil crisis that spurred national debates on energy security in the UK.
actors: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC)
events.supporting_text: In 1973, an oil export embargo of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) by major Arab oil-producing states caused a hike in the price of oil, leading an oil crisis.

events.title: Publication of The Aerosol Connection pamphlet
events.description: Friends of the Earth (FoE) in the UK published a pamphlet titled “The Aerosol Connection” listing CFC‑free aerosols and launching a publicity campaign encouraging consumers to choose them.
events.supporting_text: In 1986, the UK FoE published a pamphlet, The Aerosol Connection, detailing a list of aerosols that were CFC‑free.

events.title: Launch of FoE aerosol boycott campaign
events.description: Friends of the Earth planned to boycott best‑selling CFC‑based aerosols; the boycott was launched three days after the eight largest aerosol companies decided to phase out all CFCs by the end of 1989.
events.supporting_text: When this approach failed to persuade aerosol manufacturers to take action, FoE planned to boycott all the best‑selling CFC‑based aerosols. The eight largest aerosol companies took the decision to phase out all CFCs by the end of 1989, three days before the boycott campaign was launched.

events.title: Publication of The Green Consumer Guide
events.description: John Elkington and Julia Hailes co‑authored and published “The Green Consumer Guide”, the first book focusing on green consumer choices, selling over one million copies.
events.supporting_text: In 1988, John Elkington (b. 1949) and Julia Hailes (b. 1961) published The Green Consumer Guide, which reflected the growing interest in green consumerism and further encouraged individuals who wanted to use their purchasing power to buy the greenest products.

events.title: Launch of six new British ethical investment funds
events.description: A boom in ethical investment in the late 1980s led to the creation and launch of six new ethical funds in Britain.
events.supporting_text: In 1987 a boom in ethical investment saw the launch of six new British ethical funds.

events.title: 1989 American survey on environmental concerns of product purchases
events.description: A survey of Americans found that 89 % were concerned about the environmental impacts of the products they bought and 77 % were influenced by a company's environmental reputation.
events.supporting_text: A 1989 survey of Americans found that 89 per cent were concerned about the environmental impacts of the products they bought, while 77 per cent were influenced by a company's environmental reputation.

events.title: Organised consumer action against McDonald's
events.description: US environmental groups EDF, Earth Action Network and Kids Against Pollution launched a campaign targeting McDonald's over its waste, using tactics such as sending back wrappers and schoolchildren demonstrations.
events.supporting_text: In 1988, the US environmental groups EDF, Earth Action Network and Kids Against Pollution attacked McDonald's, the largest US fast-food chain, for the amount of rubbish it produced.

events.title: McDonald's adoption of paper‑based packaging
events.description: Following pressure on its non‑recyclable waste, McDonald's agreed to replace polystyrene clamshells with paper‑based packaging.
events.supporting_text: the company was subjected to mounting pressure on its nonrecyclable waste and in 1990 agreed to move to paper-based packaging.

events.title: Founding of The Body Shop
events.description: Anita Roddick established The Body Shop in Brighton, UK, to sell natural beauty products and promote environmentally conscious consumerism.
events.supporting_text: In 1976, Anita Roddick (1942-2007) founded The Body Shop in Brighton, UK to sell natural beauty products.

events.title: Launch of 'Save the Whale' window campaign by The Body Shop
events.description: The Body Shop, in collaboration with Greenpeace, created a window display campaign titled 'Save the Whale' to raise awareness of marine conservation.
events.supporting_text: In 1986 it created its own window campaign, 'Save the whale', in collaboration with Greenpeace.

events.title: Gallup poll on executive attitudes toward recyclable packaging
events.description: A Gallup poll revealed that 58 % of Fortune 500 executives believed customers would pay more for products with recyclable packaging or components.
events.supporting_text: A 1989 Gallup poll found that 58 per cent of Fortune magazine's 500 list of business executives believed their customers would pay more for products with recyclable packaging or components.

events.title: Survey on consumer skepticism toward environmental claims
events.description: A 1990 survey indicated that 47 % of customers dismissed environmental claims as mere 'gimmickry', reflecting growing consumer wariness of greenwashing.
events.supporting_text: One 1990 survey indicated that 47 per cent of customers dismissed environmental claims as mere 'gimmickry'.

events.title: Introduction of the EU voluntary Ecolabel scheme
events.description: The European Union launched a voluntary Ecolabel scheme to help consumers identify green products and encourage businesses to advertise environmental credentials.
events.supporting_text: One way of addressing this was through labelling, and the EU introduced a voluntary Ecolabel scheme in 1992.

events.title: Awarding of over 1,000 EU Ecolabel licences
events.description: By early 2010 more than 1,000 licences under the EU Ecolabel had been granted, with Italy and France holding the highest numbers of licence holders.
events.supporting_text: At the beginning of 2010, more than 1000 EU Ecolabel licences had been awarded, with Italy and France having the highest number of Ecolabel holders.

events.title: Tesco announcement of product carbon‑footprint labelling and emissions cut
events.description: Tesco announced it would label 70,000 products with carbon‑footprint information and aim to cut store carbon emissions by 75 %.
events.supporting_text: In 2007, Britain's leading businesses responded to a resurging green trend, with the supermarket chain Tesco announcing it would be labelling 70,000 products with details of its carbon footprint, and that it would cut carbon emissions from its stores by 75 per cent.

events.title: Marks & Spencer launch of 'Plan A' programme
events.description: Marks & Spencer launched a £200 million 'Plan A' programme aimed at making the company carbon neutral through energy reduction and increased use of recycled materials.
events.supporting_text: Marks & Spencer launched a £200 million 'Plan A' programme to make the company carbon neutral by cutting energy consumption and stocking more products from recycled materials.

events.title: Broadcast of "The Undersea World of Jacques Cousteau"
events.description: US broadcast of the television series that brought marine life to public attention for the first time.
events.supporting_text: The 1966 US broadcast of The Undersea World of Jacques Cousteau brought life under the seas to public attention for the very first time.

events.title: Release of documentary "Life on Earth"
events.description: David Attenborough produced a highly acclaimed documentary that narrated the evolution of life on the planet.
events.supporting_text: In 1979, Attenborough produced a highly acclaimed documentary, Life on Earth, which told the story of the evolution of life on the planet.

events.title: Earth Day celebration at Union Square
events.description: Actors Paul Newman and Ali McGraw participated in the 1970 Earth Day celebration in New York City.
locations: Union Square, New York City, USA
events.supporting_text: US actors Paul Newman (1925-2008) and Ali McGraw (b. 1939) took part in the 1970 Earth Day celebration at Union Square in New York City.

events.title: Live Aid concert
events.description: International artists performed at Live Aid on 13 July 1985, raising money for the Ethiopian famine and demonstrating the power of celebrity endorsement for environmentalists.
events.supporting_text: the success of the Live Aid concert on 13 July 1985 which galvanised a host of international artists to raise money to tackle the Ethiopian famine, that environmentalists realised the power of celebrity endorsement.

events.title: Founding of Rainforest Foundation International
events.description: British musician Sting, his wife Trudie Styler, and filmmaker Jean‑Pierre Dutilleux established the Rainforest Foundation International.
events.supporting_text: In 1989, British musician Sting (b. 1951) founded the Rainforest Foundation International with his wife Trudie Styler (b. 1954) and Belgian film-maker Jean-Pierre Dutilleux.

events.title: Legal recognition and demarcation of Kayapo territory
events.description: Following a campaign led by Sting and Kayapo leader Raoni Metuktire, the Brazilian government legally recognized and demarcated more than 27,359 km² of indigenous land in Amazonas.
events.supporting_text: In 1993 this resulted in legal recognition and demarcation of an area of more than 27,359 square kilometres.

events.title: Publication of Vanity Fair’s “Green Issue”
events.description: Vanity Fair released a special “Green Issue” featuring Julia Roberts, George Clooney, Al Gore and Robert Kennedy Jr., calling for a new American revolution on climate change.
events.supporting_text: In May 2006, US Vanity Fair, a magazine of popular culture, fashion and politics, reflected popular environmental awareness when it published its 'Green Issue'. The cover featured Hollywood movie stars Julia Roberts (b. 1967) and George Clooney (b. 1961), and politicians Al Gore (b. 1948) and Robert Kennedy Jr (b. 1954), dressed in complementary shades of green.

events.title: Vanity Fair abandons annual Green Issue
events.description: Three years after the Green Issue launch, Vanity Fair announced it would cease publishing the annual green issue, stating that environmental coverage had become integral to the news agenda.
events.supporting_text: Three years later, Vanity Fair announced it would abandon its annual green issue, arguing that the environment had become so integral to the news agenda that there was no longer a need for a dedicated issue.

events.title: Release of documentary "An Inconvenient Truth"
events.description: Al Gore produced the Oscar‑winning documentary that presented the scientific case for climate change and its impacts.
events.supporting_text: In 2006, former US Democratic Party Vice President Al Gore's long-standing interest in environmental issues led him to produce the Oscar-winning documentary An Inconvenient Truth.

events.title: Release of film "The Day After Tomorrow"
events.description: Hollywood science‑fiction disaster film depicting catastrophic climate‑change scenarios.
events.supporting_text: This followed the 2004 Hollywood science-fiction disaster film The Day After Tomorrow.

events.title: Release of documentary "The 11th Hour"
events.description: Leonardo DiCaprio produced and narrated a feature documentary on the state of the natural environment.
events.supporting_text: In 2007, US actor Leonardo DiCaprio (b. 1974) produced and narrated the feature film documentary The 11th Hour on the state of the natural environment.

events.title: Release of film "The Age of Stupid"
events.description: Franny Armstrong produced a drama‑documentary‑animation hybrid about climate change, starring Pete Postlethwaite.
events.supporting_text: In 2009 British environmental campaigner Franny Armstrong (b. 1972) produced the film The Age of Stupid, which continued the climate change theme.

events.title: Live Earth concert 2007
events.description: A global series of concerts calling for worldwide action to combat climate change, staged on seven continents and broadcast in 132 countries.
events.supporting_text: The 2007 Live Earth concert called for worldwide action to combat climate change across seven continents, and was broadcast in 132 countries. Described as the 'largest global entertainment event in history', Live Earth staged concerts in New York, London, Sydney, Tokyo, Shanghai, Rio de Janeiro, Johannesburg and Hamburg - as well as special broadcast events in Antarctica, Kyoto and Washington, DC.

events.title: Publication of Climate Safety report
events.description: Report by the Public Interest Research Centre concluding the need for a 10 % reduction in the developed world's emissions by the end of 2010.
events.supporting_text: In 2008, the Public Interest Research Centre's report Climate Safety concluded the need for a 10 per cent reduction in the developed world's emissions by the end of 2010.

events.title: Founding of the 10:10 campaign
events.description: Campaign encouraging individuals, businesses and organisations to commit to reducing their carbon emissions, founded by filmmaker Franny Armstrong.
events.supporting_text: This inspired Armstrong to found the 10:10 campaign, which encouraged individuals, businesses and organisations to commit to reducing their carbon emissions.

events.title: Establishment of Active Resistance project
events.description: Project set up by designer Vivienne Westwood to encourage engagement with humanitarian and environmental issues.
events.supporting_text: In 2005, the designer Vivenne Westwood (b. 1941) set up 'Active Resistance' as a project to encourage engagement with humanitarian and environmental issues.

events.title: Launch of 'I am not a plastic bag' cotton bag
events.description: An unbleached £5 cotton bag designed by Anya Hindmarch for Sainsbury's, bearing the slogan 'I am not a plastic bag', which sold out within an hour.
events.supporting_text: In 2007, bag designer Anya Hindmarch (b.1968) designed an unbleached £5 cotton bag with 'I am not a plastic bag' written on it for Sainsbury's supermarket.

events.title: Conversion of Duchy Home Farm to organic agriculture
events.description: Process begun by Prince Charles in the early 1980s to convert the Duchy Home Farm on the Highgrove estate to an organic agricultural system.
events.supporting_text: In the early 1980s, when Prince Charles moved to the Highgrove estate in Gloucestershire, he began the process of converting the Duchy Home Farm, which is part of the estate, to an organic agricultural system.

events.title: Launch of Duchy Originals organic brand
events.description: Prince Charles launched his own organic brand, Duchy Originals, to produce natural, organic products and support countryside and wildlife protection.
events.supporting_text: In 1990, he launched his own organic brand, Duchy Originals, which embodies the Prince of Wales's commitment to producing natural, organic products while helping to protect and sustain the countryside and wildlife.

events.title: Setting of household carbon emissions reduction target
events.description: Prince Charles's household set a target to reduce its carbon emissions by 25 % by 2012, using 2007 as the baseline year.
events.supporting_text: In 2007, his household set a target to reduce its carbon emissions by 25 per cent by 2012 against a baseline year of 2007.

events.title: Prince Charles speech to the European Parliament
events.description: First speech by Prince Charles to the European Parliament, calling for EU leadership in the war against climate change.
events.supporting_text: Following this, in his first speech to the European Parliament on 14 February 2008, the Prince called for EU leadership in the war against climate change.

events.title: Prince Charles BBC lecture on climate change
events.description: BBC lecture where Prince Charles argued that people must change their behaviour to stop the effects of climate change.
events.supporting_text: He also used a 2009 BBC lecture to argue that it is essential that people change their behaviour to stop the effects of climate change.

events.title: Royal Train ecotour and sustainability festival
events.description: Prince Charles undertook a bio‑fuel‑powered Royal Train ecotour across the UK to promote sustainable living, culminating in a sustainability festival attended by about 70,000 people.
events.supporting_text: The Prince's activities continued in 2010, when he undertook an ecotour of the UK in a bio-fuel-powered Royal Train to promote an initiative to encourage and celebrate sustainable living. At the end of the tour, he held a sustainability festival attended by an estimated 70,000 people and demonstrated how everyone could make a difference.

events.title: First Earth Day
events.description: In the USA, public concern for the environment first peaked around the first Earth Day in 1970 and then declined over the following decade.
events.supporting_text: In the USA, public concern for the environment first peaked around the first Earth Day in 1970 and then declined over the following decade.

events.title: Time magazine declares “Endangered Earth” Planet of the Year
events.description: In 1989, the US Time magazine declared “Endangered Earth” as the “Planet of the Year” instead of its usual man or woman of the year.
events.supporting_text: In 1989, the US Time magazine declared 'Endangered Earth' as the 'Planet of the Year' instead of its usual man or woman of the year.

events.title: Environment ranked fourth on national priorities list
events.description: The environment ranked fourth on a 1990 list of national priorities.
events.supporting_text: The environment ranked fourth on a 1990 list of national priorities.

events.title: Climategate controversy
events.description: The November 2009 “climategate” controversy over climate science contributed to a decline in public concern about climate change.
events.supporting_text: The November 2009 'climategate' controversy over climate science (see Chapter 4) contributed to a decline in public concern about climate change.

events.title: 2010 public attitudes survey in England
events.description: A 2010 survey of public attitudes in England revealed that the majority of the public still believed that the climate is changing and were prepared to take action.
events.supporting_text: A 2010 survey of public attitudes in England revealed that the majority of the public still believed that the climate is changing and were prepared to take action.

events.title: Increase in environmental concern during the 1980s
events.description: The 1980s saw an increase in environmental concern with the discovery of climate change, the ozone hole and an increase in environmental disasters such as the Union Carbide gas tragedy in India, the Chernobyl nuclear disaster and the Exxon Valdez oil spill.
events.supporting_text: The 1980s saw an increase in environmental concern with the discovery of climate change, the ozone hole and an increase in environmental disasters such as the Union Carbide gas tragedy in India, the Chernobyl nuclear disaster and the Exxon Valdez oil spill.

events.title: Rapid growth of US public concern for the environment (1987‑1990)
events.description: US public concern for the environment grew much more quickly than any other issue in the period 1987‑90.
events.supporting_text: US public concern for the environment grew much more quickly than any other issue in the period 1987-90.

events.title: 2009 EU study on European public attitudes to climate change
events.description: A European Union‑commissioned survey that found two‑thirds of Europeans considered climate change a very serious problem, while highlighting gaps in knowledge in several member states.
events.supporting_text: A 2009 EU study found that two‑thirds of Europeans felt the climate is a very serious problem. In Turkey, Romania, Bulgaria and Lithuania, citizens felt they were not well informed about the causes and effects of climate change.

events.title: 2010 Yale University study of US public attitudes to climate change
events.description: A Yale University survey that reported 63 % of Americans believed global warming is happening, identified knowledge gaps and misconceptions, and measured trust in scientists and desire for more education on climate change.
events.supporting_text: A 2010 Yale University study of US public attitudes to climate change found that 63 per cent of Americans believed that global warming is happening. The study also found gaps in knowledge and common misconceptions about climate change.

events.title: Publication of "Sizzle: The New Climate Message" report
events.description: A report by the sustainability communications consultancy Futerra that argues campaigns should focus on a positive, appealing vision of a greener life to re‑engage the public and media.
events.supporting_text: A report by the sustainability communications consultancy Futerra, Sizzle: The New Climate Message, argues that in order to reinvigorate public and media interest, campaigns need to focus on a vision of a greener life that is positive and appealing to all.

events.title: 2009 UK survey on green lifestyle attitudes
events.description: A national survey that revealed public confusion about what constitutes a green lifestyle, showing mixed attitudes toward personal environmental impact and guilt about harmful behaviours.
events.supporting_text: This confusion about what a green lifestyle actually entails is evident in the responses to a 2009 UK survey on the issue.

events.title: Development of environmentalism within popular culture
events.description: A multi‑decadal process, beginning in the 1960s, through which environmentalism entered mainstream Western culture, acquiring a counter‑cultural element and influencing media, consumerism, and celebrity discourse.
events.supporting_text: This chapter has examined how environmentalism developed as part of popular culture over the past sixty years. In the 1960s, environmental issues burst into the public consciousness with unprecedented speed and urgency.
